text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet decided to impose maximum price limits for basic foods in a move to counter profiteering amid rising inflation sparked by a falling lev and economic instability.

-- Bulgaria's national carrier Balkan Airlines plans to suspend flights to and from Brussels, Helsinki, Stockholm and Harare during the winter if they prove to be loss-making, company officials said. @

-- Bulgaria's cabinet approved draft amendments to the foreign investment law, extending a five-year tax holiday for non-fiscal foreign investments like machines and equipment, patent rights, licences, technologies and know-how in a bid to speed up privatisation, a government official said.
-- Bulgaria's Industry Ministry is expected to open a liquidation procedure for the forklift truck producer Balkankar Holding by the end of this week, Industry minister Lyubomir Dachev said. @
South Korea's industrial giant Daewoo is expected to start talks on September 20 with the ministry about buying a stake in Balkankar, Dachev said.

-- Russia is expected on September 16 to start delivering natural gas to Greece via Bulgaria under an agreement between the Russian gas giant Gazprom, Bulgaria's Bulgargas and the Greek national gas distributor Depa, Balkan agency reported. @

-- Bulgaria is expected to start negotiations with the World Bank on September 29 for a loan for the construction of a five-star Hilton hotel in Bulgaria's capital, a Sofia municipality official said.
-- South Korea's industrial giant Daewoo plans to assemble cars in one of Bulgaria's duty-free zones, an Industry ministry official said, declining to elaborate.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet has not discussed a new budget revision, Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov said, rejecting local media reports. The budget was revised in July this year. @

-- Bulgaria's central bank allowed commercial banks to hold in foreign currency up to 100 percent of minimum required reserves at the BNB on attracted foreign currency deposits to stimulate banks to attract such deposits.

So far banks had to convert into levs the minimum required reserves on foreign exchange deposits which incurred losses to them due to the lev's fall on the domestic forex market. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
